Opening NIS data

Source: vignettes/articles/opening-data.Rmd
opening-data.Rmd

Use the synthetic fixture

nis_example() creates an invented Parquet dataset with familiar NIS fields. It is suitable for learning and examples, not for estimating national quantities.

path <- nis_example(years = 2019:2020)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpHUuVgN/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpHUuVgN/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
nis <- nis_open(path)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpHUuVgN/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
nis |> dplyr::count(YEAR) |> dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>    YEAR     n
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1  2020    96
#> 2  2019    96

The result reports the number of synthetic rows in each selected year.

Select years and columns

years limits which annual files are opened. Use dplyr::select() to narrow what a later collection needs; lazy operations are evaluated when collected.

nis_open(path, years = 2020) |>
  dplyr::select(YEAR, AGE, FEMALE, LOS) |>
  dplyr::collect() |>
  head()
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpHUuVgN/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>    YEAR   AGE FEMALE   LOS
#>   <int> <dbl>  <int> <dbl>
#> 1  2020    28      1     2
#> 2  2020    35      0     3
#> 3  2020    42      1     4
#> 4  2020    49      0     5
#> 5  2020    56      1     6
#> 6  2020    63      0     7

The preview contains only the requested variables from the synthetic 2020 file. Mixed-case column names are normalized to upper case; already lower-case names remain unchanged.

Filter and project before collecting

nis_open() uses DuckDB’s native Parquet reader and returns a lazy dbplyr table. duckdb, dbplyr, and DBI are required dependencies. Filter and select before collecting when later analysis needs an in-memory data frame.

duck <- nis_open(path, years = 2020)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpHUuVgN/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
duck |> dplyr::count(YEAR) |> dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>    YEAR     n
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1  2020    96

This count is the same synthetic year summary, evaluated through DuckDB.

Common pitfalls

Common pitfalls

  • Opening all years and collecting all columns can require substantial memory. Filter and select before collecting.
  • Survey-design preparation collects the selected design fields in R. Keep the cohort and retained columns bounded before using nis_design().
  • nis_example() data are invented and should not be reported as NIS estimates.

See Cohort definitions, nis_open(), and nis_example().
